market_holds: Spot $8.185 (sealed 2026-11-13 18:13 UTC; Yahoo daily close $8.00 on a 1.0M-share day, about 5x the 20-day average of ~199k). The stock is -58% from its post-emergence high ($20 intraday on 2026-08-10, first day) and -11.8% over 20 sessions, but +8.55% over 5 sessions after a $6.90 low on 2026-10-30. It slid from ~$16 in mid-September to ~$7 by late October on no company news I could find. Peers did not cause it: the move is this name's own. There is no option chain, no analyst coverage (Google Finance/Benzinga list none) and no consensus, and the company gives no guidance. The deadband is 5.48% (one day at 87% realised vol). The capital structure per the 424B3 dated 2026-10-01: 49,999,897 shares, so equity is about $410M; $1.325B of takeback debt per the plan. About 74% was held by four distressed funds at emergence (SVP 26.2%, Silver Point 17.3%, GoldenTree 15.7%, Oaktree 14.4%). 37.6M shares were registered for resale, effective 2026-09-29. On the last full data (Q2 10-Q, filed 2026-08-04), QVC revenue was down ~8-11% in constant currency and QVC Adjusted OIBDA was $152M vs $225M (-32%), with H1 down ~$117M. FY2025 OIBDA is roughly $770-830M (secondary sources disagree). So EV is about $1.5-1.7B, roughly 2.5-3x a run-rate that is falling 30%. The price assumes continued steep deterioration. Short interest is small: 425k shares, 0.8% (FINRA 2026-10-30). The release is a 10-Q plus a posted audio review, not a press release with guidance.
view: This is the first quarter reported as a post-reorganization equity, with fresh-start accounting and a predecessor/successor split. Nobody covers it and it trades on a small float. The October collapse (-45% from $12.35 to $6.90 in three weeks) lines up with supply rather than news. The resale shelf for 37.6M shares went effective on 2026-09-29. Silver Point sold 1.6M shares to GoldenTree at $16.25 on 09-08 and 1.352M at $12.35 on 10-09, which took it to 4.95M shares (9.9%). Below 10% its further sales no longer need a Form 4, so an invisible seller of up to ~5M shares into a ~150k-a-day market can explain the slide. GoldenTree bought at $12.35-16.25 and has filed no purchase since 10-09. Against that, the business trend is genuinely bad: QxH units are falling, Q2 OIBDA was -32%, and the debtor-level MORs show QVC, Inc. sales of $313.8M in June and $295.8M in July. The line the stock will trade on is whether Q3 OIBDA decline narrows (H1 cost savings, lower returns) or widens, plus post-emergence cash and leverage. Neither is visible before the release. At ~2.5-3x falling OIBDA, a print that merely repeats Q2's trend probably clears the bar, so a relief move is slightly more likely than not. A worse trend, or heavy reorg costs read as weakness, could take it to new lows. The bigger problem is timing. Recent 10-Qs on this CIK were accepted at 08:34 ET (2026-05-15), 14:25 ET (2026-08-04), 16:18 ET (2025-11-05) and 13:35 ET (2025-08-07), so the filing has perhaps a 40-50% chance of landing before the 13:00 ET Monday exit. If it lands later, the window is only Friday-close-to-Monday-midday noise on an 87%-vol name.
unpriced: Possibly the technical part of the October decline: holders selling down after the resale registration, with Silver Point dropping below the Form 4 line, rather than new information about the business. If the 10-Q shows the trend no worse than Q2, the price is below what the company's own evidence supports. This is a hypothesis I cannot prove from public data, and I cannot show what the price assumes about Q3.

recommendation.reason: The October fall looks driven by supply (resale shelf effective 09-29, a seller dropping below the Form 4 threshold) and the valuation is depressed, which leans the print slightly upward. But there is no consensus, no guide and no visible Q3 datapoint to say which side of the OIBDA line the quarter lands on. Roughly half the time the 10-Q will land after the 13:00 ET Monday exit. That is not a mechanism worth betting on.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q3 10-Q filed before the open showing QxH revenue decline accelerating to double digits, Adjusted OIBDA down more than Q2's -32%, or post-emergence cash/liquidity below expectations would make the down side more likely. A pre-market filing with OIBDA decline narrowing toward -15-20% would make a long tenable.

self_critique: Sophisticated distressed holders own most of the stock. A slide from $12 to $7 after quarter-end may reflect informed selling on a weak Q3 (for example, QxH declines accelerating with tariffs and cord-cutting), not just mechanical supply. GoldenTree stopped buying after 10-09 despite the price halving. Fresh-start and reorganization charges can produce ugly GAAP headlines that a no-coverage name trades on. And with a ~50% chance the filing misses the window, any lean is diluted toward noise.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped: the slide was this name's own and lined up with the resale shelf and block sales rather than news. P7's push to estimate the line from inputs had little to work with here: no consensus, no guide, only debtor-level MORs. The window/timing check (definition rule 1) mattered more than anything in the playbook.
